premise.claim: Today that propagation is un-paced: when the template changes, every outdated child is updated within a single reconcile, with no ordering and no availability gating. For a set of N groups that means all N groups can restart at once.
premise.evidence: On merge-base fc201cdf a single Reconcile rewrote all 3 outdated children onto the new template at once (results/premise-base.txt). Run: bash docs/verification/pr474-rbgs-rolling-update/scripts/verify-premise.sh

findings.note: TestVerify_F1_NegativeMaxUnavailableWedgesRollout is a mechanism demo of the controller-side wedge (budget = -1 + readySurge); it passes before and after the admission fix unless the controller also gains clamping.
The PR's own TestRoleBasedGroupSetValidator_ScalingAdapterCreateOnly pins the disputed behavior (newly-enabled adapter allowed on update) and must be updated when the fix lands.

Consistency contract: Rolling=RolloutComplete must agree with surge release. Satisfied by either scoping completion to serving base groups (status side) or scoping serving to in-scope ordinals (surge side).

liveNote: No live layer was run (debate setup runs unit + integration only). If a live pass is wanted: on a real cluster create an RBGS with rolloutStrategy maxUnavailable=1, change groupTemplate, and watch that exactly one child RoleBasedGroup is deleted/recreated at a time (integration spec I3 is the envtest analogue and passes today).
